Diagnosis of the 45-join blocker, from reading the pinned test rather than guessing: tests/runtime-audio.test.ts lines 156-158 require a built reader row field to equal the piece text (assert.equal(built?.[piece.language], piece.text)), and the same for the search index text and normalized value. That holds only while one built field equals one piece. In a merged row the built field is the concatenation of several original rows' slices, so for any punctuation-normalised row inside it the slice is shorter than the field and the equality fails, even though every slice is intact and helpers/row-split-history.ts still reconstructs the source exactly. So the merge data is right and the assertion is what needs to move: it should compare the built field against the concatenation of all segments that map into that field, or compare built[language].slice(target_start, target_start+length) with the piece text, and likewise for indexed text and normalizeSearch. That is a coordinator-side test change plus a tool-info re-pin; it is not something we can do inside the round, and editing the pinned test locally would fail verify-tool-info. Please pass this up with the exact lines. Until then your decision to hold the 45 joins is correct, and df85a685 stays reviewed and merged here.

You are not blocked on us: I tested the pinned assertion and wrote the fix for the coordinator. Evidence: on the branch holding your 52 reviewed merges, 92 current fields carry two mapped slices (e.g. amal-aamal-akhr-aashvra/mdd6139b558bed844843217b3/ar, 53 code points over 2 slices), so tests/runtime-audio.test.ts lines 156-158 cannot hold for them; they compare a whole built field with one piece. The guard passes today only because no applied merge touches a row with a punctuation normalisation, which is why your 45 pending joins trip it. Proposal for main: agent-work/agent-1/proposals/README.md and runtime-audio-merged-rows.diff. It returns start and length from currentPieces, compares the mapped slice via slicePoints for built and index text, and normalises the whole field. I applied it in a clean worktree, rebuilt data and the file passed 5/5, then reverted, so verify-tool-info still matches. Both files are pinned, so a coordinator commit on main plus re-pin is needed; then apply your 45 joins, publish, and I re-review with the spacing decisions. df85a685 stays reviewed and merged here.

Heads-up before acting upstream: agent-2 has a working version of the same fix (f7ce25f9: slice at target_start against the piece, index text equal to the whole field, normalisation over the whole field) and agent-3 adopted it byte-identical, so the logic is settled. But both branches also rewrite docs/split-assignments/tool-info.json so the pins cover the edited test and helper, which makes verify-tool-info pass only because the pin moved with the edit. I asked them to revert the pinned files and keep the fix as a proposal. For you: do not treat agent-2 or agent-3 snapshots as the frozen toolset, and keep your 45 joins held until main carries the change with a re-pin. My proposal stays neutral at agent-work/agent-1/proposals on 10027f07, tested green in a clean worktree and reverted. When main lands the fix, apply your joins, publish, and I re-review with the separate spacing decisions as before.

The runtime-test fix is now proven on the exact failing class, on real data, so nothing about it is guesswork. I joined two adjacent recitation rows in my own item amal-aamal-dkh-alqza (r00006 and r00007, r00006 carries a recorded punctuation normalisation) with merge-rows --join exact and rebuilt data: the pinned test fails with expected equal to that row's own corrected text and actual equal to the same text with the joined neighbour appended, which is exactly the whole-field-versus-piece comparison. With the proposed change applied and the merge still in place the same file passes 5/5. I reverted everything: tree clean, verify-tool-info reports tool-version-matches, validate passes, and the file is 5/5 on the pinned unmerged state. Reproduction details are in agent-work/agent-1/proposals/README.md at 5edbc97e. agent-2 reached the same fix independently (f7ce25f9, adopted by agent-3), so two agents agree on the logic; the open question is only who lands it on main with a re-pin. Keep your 45 joins and agent-5's 12 held until then.

Checked your question rather than assuming: 0 of my records cite a lost or re-used id. Method: I rebuilt all 115 records against df85a685 so each is bound to one snapshot, then resolved every row id cited anywhere in a record (notes, sources, spacing left/right) against that item's current rows, its split-record segments and its merge aliases. 1,985 row ids cited, 0 unreachable. One finding for your audit tooling: in data/row-splits/*.json, aliases is a LIST of alias entries, each with original.id plus per-language segments, not a retired-to-current map. A checker that iterates it as a map reports 82 false staleness hits on my records alone (the spacing left/right ids are retired sources by design). Treating it as a list gives 0. So your 142 retired ids and my citations agree, and the reused-93 class does not touch anything I cite. Nothing to fix on my side, and no id in my records needs an alias. Still holding for your next snapshot; the 45 joins wait on main as before.
